key_insight: The paper introduces a high-order finite-difference framework that preserves special relativistic hydrodynamics physical constraints by converting nonlinear admissibility conditions into solvable linear inequalities and enforcing them with a flux limiter.
engineering_relevance: This enables robust, accurate simulations of extreme relativistic flows without violating positivity or subluminal-speed constraints, which is critical for shock-dominated and astrophysical CFD applications.
method: Uses geometric quasilinearization (GQL) to reformulate RHD constraints as linear inequalities.
Integrates a Zalesak-type flux-corrected transport limiter directly on conservative variables in a finite-difference WENO scheme.
Computes limiting parameters non-iteratively via stereographic parameterization and small symmetric eigenvalue problems.
evidence_signal: The method is validated on numerical benchmarks from 1D to 3D, including ultra-relativistic Riemann problems and astrophysical jets, showing robustness, sharp discontinuity capture, and design-order accuracy on smooth solutions.
watch_item: The PCP guarantee relies on solving extra eigenvalue problems and special limiting formulations, so implementation cost and complexity may increase in multidimensional simulations.
paper_title: GQL-Based Physical-Constraint-Preserving High-Order Finite Difference Schemes for Special Relativistic Hydrodynamics in Arbitrary Dimensions
